correctness.rationale: For positive q-periodic weights the normalized diagonal \(c_{j+1}=c_jw_j/\gamma\) closes every q steps and has uniformly bounded inverse. Exact conjugacy \(W=\gamma DSD^{-1}\) yields power decay at \(\gamma<1\), divergence on every nonzero vector at \(\gamma>1\), and q exact orbit-norm phases at \(\gamma=1\). The shift \(S^n\) converges weakly to zero, which removes all asymptotic cross terms and makes the minimum-over-residues necessary and sufficient for syndetic base-point returns. Exact rational-radical witness checks show two AP_1 vectors with a midpoint outside all phase ellipsoids. A clean extracted checker verifies 240 finite phase identities; finite evidence is auxiliary, not the reason infinite quantifiers hold.

value.rationale: This classifies base-point syndetic recurrence radii for every positive periodic forward shift, including all vectors and the complete period-product phase diagram. The critical formula yields an explicit finite union of Hilbert ellipsoids and, already at period two, a rigorous nonconvexity counterexample for a power-bounded operator similar to an isometry. This separates noncontractive similarity classes from contraction geometry and supplies a natural sharp structural boundary, rather than just a cheap numerical check or routine restatement. Subcritical and supercritical elementary regimes are included for completeness, not claimed as separate discoveries.
